policy_name: California Assembly Bill 2905 (Telecommunications: automatic dialing-announcing devices: artificial voices) (2024)
question: How might businesses using automatic dialing-announcing devices need to alter their operational procedures to comply with the requirement of disclosing the use of an artificial voice?
answer_low_temp:
Businesses using automatic dialing-announcing devices in California will need to alter their operational procedures to comply with the requirement of disclosing the use of an artificial voice. This is because the amended Section 2874 of the Public Utilities Code now requires that if a prerecorded message uses an artificial voice, it must be explicitly stated in the announcement made to the person called by the person calling (Sec. 1, subsection c, paragraph 3). This disclosure is in addition to the existing requirements for the announcement to state the nature of the call, the name, address, and telephone number of the business or organization being represented, and to inquire as to whether the person called consents to hear the prerecorded message (Sec. 1, subsection a, paragraphs 1, 2). The amended section defines "artificial voice" as a voice that is generated or significantly altered using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, subsection c, paragraph 2).

Citation: California Legislative Information. (2023). Public Utilities Code - PUC § 2874. Retrieved from https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PUC&sectionNum=2874

The announcement must inform the person called if the prerecorded message uses an artificial voice (Section 2874(a)(3)). Failure to comply with this requirement may result in penalties or fines, as the amendment creates a new infraction within the meaning of Section 17556 of the Government Code.
